overview.historicalContext: Erdős posed Problem #539 in [Er73] (1973), asking about the minimum size of {a/gcd(a,b) : a,b ∈ A} over all n-element sets A ⊆ N. Erdős-Szemerédi established n^{1/2} ≪ h(n) ≪ n^{1-c}, Freiman-Lev improved the upper bound to n^{2/3}, and Granville-Roesler provided a geometric reformulation. The exact behavior of h(n) remains unknown, with the true exponent between 1/2 and 2/3. The study of GCD-reduced quotients connects to the multiplicative structure of integer sets and to Freiman-type theorems in additive combinatorics, which characterize sets with small sumsets as approximate arithmetic progressions. The geometric reformulation by Granville and Roesler relates the problem to lattice point distributions and convex geometry.
overview.problemStatement:
**Problem Statement (Open)**

Let h(n) be such that for any set A ⊆ ℕ of size n, the set
{ a / gcd(a,b) : a, b ∈ A }
has size at least h(n). Estimate h(n).

**Known Bounds:**
- Lower: h(n) ≫ n^{1/2} (Erdős-Szemerédi)
- Upper: h(n) ≪ n^{2/3} (Freiman-Lev)

The gap between 1/2 and 2/3 remains open.

overview.proofStrategy:
**Formalization Approach**

1. **GCD Quotient:** gcdQuotient a b = a / gcd(a,b)

2. **Quotient Set:** gcdQuotientSet A = { gcdQuotient a b : a,b ∈ A }

3. **The Function:** h(n) = infimum of quotient set sizes

4. **Lower Bound:** erdos_szemeredi_lower (n^{1/2})

5. **Upper Bounds:** erdos_szemeredi_upper (n^{1-c}), freiman_lev_upper (n^{2/3})

6. **Examples:** APs and GPs have specific quotient set sizes

7. **Geometric View:** Granville-Roesler reformulation

sections.title: Problem Overview and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring stating Erdős Problem #539 (estimate h(n), the minimum size of {a/gcd(a,b) : a,b ∈ A} over n-element A ⊆ ℕ), the known Erdős-Szemerédi and Freiman-Lev bounds and references, the Nat/Finset/Real imports, open Finset BigOperators Nat, and namespace Erdos539.
sections.mathContext: $h(n)$ is the largest value such that every $n$-element $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ has $|\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a,b \in A\}| \ge h(n)$. Known: $n^{1/2} \ll h(n) \ll n^{2/3}$.

sections.title: Part I: The GCD-Reduced Quotient Set
sections.summary: gcdQuotient a b = a / gcd(a,b) and its basic properties: gcdQuotient_pos (positive for a,b>0) and gcdQuotient_is_nat (gcdQuotient·gcd = a). Defines gcdQuotientSet (the image over A×A) and gcdQuotientSize (its cardinality).
sections.mathContext: The reduced quotient $a/\gcd(a,b)$ is a positive integer; the quotient set is $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : (a,b) \in A \times A\}$.

sections.title: Part II: The Function h(n)
sections.summary: Defines h(n) as the infimum of gcdQuotientSize over all n-element positive sets. Theorems: quotient_set_nonempty, gcdQuotient_self (= 1 for a>0), and one_in_quotient_set (1 always lies in the quotient set).
sections.mathContext: $h(n) = \min_{|A|=n} |\{a/\gcd(a,b)\}|$. Since $a/\gcd(a,a)=1$, the value $1$ always belongs to the quotient set.

sections.title: Part III: Erdős-Szemerédi Bounds
sections.summary: ErdosSzemeredi_Bounds: the proposition packaging the original bounds n^{1/2} ≪ h(n) ≪ n^{1-c} for some c>0.
sections.mathContext: Erdős-Szemerédi: $\exists c_1>0,\ h(n) \ge c_1 n^{1/2}$ and $\exists\, 0<c_2<1,\ h(n) \le n^{1-c_2}$.

sections.title: Part IV: Freiman-Lev Improvement
sections.summary: ImprovedBounds: the proposition encoding the improved upper bound h(n) ≪ n^{2/3} alongside the n^{1/2} lower bound.
sections.mathContext: Freiman-Lev sharpen the upper bound to $h(n) \le C n^{2/3}$, narrowing the window to $n^{1/2} \ll h(n) \ll n^{2/3}$.

sections.title: Part V: Examples
sections.summary: Extremal example constructions: arithmeticProgression {a,2a,…,na} and geometricProgression {a^0,…,a^{n-1}}, which produce small quotient sets.
sections.mathContext: Arithmetic progressions $\{a, 2a, \dots, na\}$ and geometric progressions $\{a^i\}$ are candidate extremal sets minimizing the quotient set size.

sections.title: Part VI: Connection to GCD Structure
sections.summary: gcdMatrix and quotientMatrix: the GCD matrix (i,j) ↦ gcd(i,j) and the quotient matrix (i,j) ↦ gcdQuotient i j restricted to A, linking the problem to GCD-matrix structure.
sections.mathContext: The quotient set is encoded by the entries of the GCD/quotient matrices $(\gcd(i,j))$ and $(i/\gcd(i,j))$ indexed by $A$.

sections.title: Part VII: Geometric Reformulation (Granville-Roesler)
sections.summary: Docstring marker for the Granville-Roesler geometric reformulation of the quotient-set problem (no Lean declarations in this part).
sections.mathContext: Granville-Roesler recast $h(n)$ geometrically via lattice-point/dilation structure of the set $A$.

sections.title: Part VIII: Special Sets with Small Quotient Sets
sections.summary: extremalSets: the proposition asserting that for every n≥2 there is an n-element positive set whose quotient-set size is at most n^{2/3}, witnessing the upper bound.
sections.mathContext: $\forall n \ge 2,\ \exists A,\ |A|=n,\ |\text{quotientSet}(A)| \le n^{2/3}$ — extremal sets realizing the Freiman-Lev upper bound.

sections.title: Part IX: The Erdős Question
sections.summary: ErdosQuestion539 (does h(n)=Θ(n^α) for some α∈[1/2,2/3]?) and openExponentQuestion (is the true exponent near 2/3?), formalizing the open problem.
sections.mathContext: Open: is $h(n) = \Theta(n^\alpha)$ for a single $\alpha \in [1/2, 2/3]$? Extremal evidence hints $\alpha$ may be $2/3$.

sections.title: Part X: Summary
sections.summary: Closing summary docstring restating the OPEN status, the lower bound n^{1/2} (Erdős-Szemerédi) and upper bound n^{2/3} (Freiman-Lev), and the closing of namespace Erdos539.
sections.mathContext: Status OPEN: bounds $n^{1/2} \ll h(n) \ll n^{2/3}$ established; the exact growth exponent is unknown.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #539 asks for the minimum size of { a/gcd(a,b) : a,b ∈ A } over n-element sets. Erdős-Szemerédi proved n^{1/2} ≪ h(n) ≪ n^{1-c}, and Freiman-Lev improved the upper bound to n^{2/3}. The exact exponent remains unknown.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Connections**

1. **Additive Combinatorics:** GCD structure relates to sum-product phenomena

**2. Divisibility:** Quotients encode divisibility relationships

3. **Geometric Interpretation:** Granville-Roesler's lattice point view

4. **Extremal Sets:** Special structure needed for small quotient sets.
openQuestions: What is the true exponent α in h(n) = Θ(n^α)?
Is h(n) closer to n^{1/2} or n^{2/3}?
What is the structure of extremal sets?
Can the lower bound be improved?
